sourcedFrom: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 (UNKNOWN — no year printed; the cover's edition code reads AP & KAP 1/03 C R8)
cleanIntro: The Mark II strips in Ruger's fixed order: hammer down, the mainspring housing swings out and takes the bolt stop pin with it, the bolt drops out muzzle-up, and a plastic-hammer blow takes the barrel-receiver off the grip frame. Ruger stops there and reserves everything further to the factory; the one deeper procedure the book publishes is the magazine strip. Reassembly is where these pistols fight back, and the book spends four pages on it.

steps.title: Magazine out, bolt back, look in the chamber
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, fingers outside the trigger guard, safety on if the pistol is cocked. Remove the magazine. Draw the bolt fully to the rear by its ears, look into the chamber, the receiver and the magazine well to be certain no cartridge is there, then release the bolt.
steps.prose: A cartridge left in the chamber still fires with the magazine out, and a round that was not flung clear can drop into the magazine well instead. Look at all three places, and if the bolt went back gently, look twice.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine. Draw the bolt fully rearward and visually inspect the chamber to be certain there is no cartridge in it and then release the bolt.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Disassembly, step 1, p.20
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly or assembly.

steps.title: Safety off, trigger pulled — hammer down
steps.action: Push the safety down to the "off" (F) position, point the pistol in a safe direction and pull the trigger so the hammer falls. The magazine stays out for this pull: the book's disassembly never puts it back.
steps.prose: Nothing else comes apart with the hammer cocked, so this is not optional. Ruger says the pistol may be dry fired as long as the firing pin stop is in place, so the pull itself does no harm.
steps.quote: Place the safety in the “off” (F) position. Point the pistol in a safe direction and pull the trigger, to be sure hammer has fallen. Hammer must be uncocked before pistol can be disassembled.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Disassembly, step 1, p.20

steps.title: Open the mainspring housing latch
steps.action: Find the oval recess in the mainspring housing at the back of the grip. Put a blunt pointed instrument into it and swing the housing latch open, the way the blade of a pocket knife opens.
steps.prose: Ruger's own suggestion for the tool is a paper clip looped over the latch, which is what most owners end up using. Anything sharp will mark the housing.
steps.quote: Insert a blunt, ‘pointed’ instrument in the oval recess of the mainspring housing (at the back of the grip) and swing the housing latch open like the blade of a pocket knife.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Disassembly, step 2, p.20

steps.title: Housing and bolt stop pin out together
steps.action: Swing the whole housing outward on its pivot and pull it downward. The mainspring housing and the bolt stop pin come out as one assembly. On a new pistol you may need to tap lightly, with a plastic hammer, on the top of the bolt stop pin where it stands above the receiver while you pull down on the housing.
steps.prose: The pin rides with the housing; do not go looking for it separately. If it will not come, the taps are light ones with a plastic hammer, never steel.
steps.quote: Swing the entire housing outward on its pivot and pull downward, removing mainspring housing and bolt stop pin.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Disassembly, step 3, p.20

steps.title: Muzzle up — the bolt comes out
steps.action: Point the muzzle up. The bolt drops out of the back of the receiver, or slides out easily by hand.
steps.prose: With the bolt stop pin gone there is nothing holding the bolt; gravity does the work. Catch it rather than letting it fall onto a hard bench, and keep the small firing pin stop in mind, because reassembly depends on it.
steps.quote: Point muzzle up. The bolt will drop out of the receiver or it can readily be removed.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Disassembly, step 4, p.20

steps.title: Barrel-receiver off the grip frame
steps.action: With the housing and pin assembly and the bolt out, strike the rear of the receiver forward with a plastic hammer. The barrel-receiver assembly comes off the front of the grip frame.
steps.prose: The order in that sentence is the precondition: the housing, the pin and the bolt all have to be out first. A plastic hammer, not a steel one, and the blow goes on the rear of the receiver.
steps.quote: With the mainspring housing, bolt stop pin (as an assembly), and bolt removed, a forward blow (with a plastic hammer) on the rear of the receiver will disengage the barrel-receiver assembly from the grip frame.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Disassembly, step 5, p.20

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Four groups: the grip frame, the barrel-receiver, the bolt, and the mainspring housing with its bolt stop pin. Ruger forbids taking out rivets or staked pins and reserves anything further to the factory.
steps.prose: This is the extent Ruger's cleaning section sends you to: from here the bore, the chamber, the bolt face, the extractor and the feed ramp are all reachable. The magazine strip is the one deeper procedure this book publishes, and it sits behind Deep Clean.
steps.quote: No attempt should be made to remove rivets or staked pins. Further disassembly should be undertaken only by the factory.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Disassembly, step 5, p.20

deepSteps.title: Magazine empty, held upside down
deepSteps.action: Take the magazine out of the pistol, remove every cartridge from it and check the chamber again. Hold the magazine upside down in your left hand so the hole in the magazine block is where you can reach it.
deepSteps.prose: Ruger strips the magazine only when it is dirty, so this is a sometimes job, not every clean. Point the bottom of the magazine away from people and anything breakable before going further.
deepSteps.quote: Withdraw magazine from pistol and remove all cartridges (Check chamber to be certain no cartridge remains in it). Hold magazine upside down in left hand so that the hole in the Magazine Block is accessible.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Magazine Disassembly, p.24

deepSteps.title: Plunger down, block forward under control
deepSteps.action: Push a drift punch into the hole and press the magazine block retaining plunger in about 1/4". Slide the magazine block forward slowly, keeping the plunger and spring under control, until the block is fully off. Then ease the plunger and spring out.
deepSteps.prose: The spring is under load and the plunger rides on it. Let the block move a little at a time with your thumb over it, never all at once.
deepSteps.quote: Slide Magazine Block forward slowly BEING VERY CAREFUL TO KEEP PLUNGER AND SPRING UNDER CONTROL.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Magazine Disassembly, steps 1-3, p.24
deepSteps.warn: If not contained, these parts will fly out with considerable force. Therefore keep bottom end of magazine pointed away from persons and objects.

deepSteps.title: Follower button, then the follower
deepSteps.action: Lay the magazine flat in your left hand. Line the magazine follower button up with the circular opening near the bottom of the magazine body and lift the button out. The follower then comes out.
deepSteps.prose: The button only leaves through that one opening, so slide it along until it lines up rather than forcing it. With the parts out, Ruger's instruction is a thorough cleaning of the magazine.
deepSteps.quote: Now, holding magazine flat in left hand, align the Magazine Follower Button with circular opening near the lower end of magazine body and lift out the Magazine Follower Button.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Magazine Disassembly, steps 4-5, p.24

deepSteps.title: Back together in reverse, then test the follower
deepSteps.action: Rebuild in reverse order: follower, follower button, spring and plunger, then slide the magazine bottom on and lock it, holding the spring and plunger in as it goes. When it is together, run the follower button up and down with your thumb to check it moves freely.
deepSteps.prose: The spring and plunger are the same hazard going back in as coming out. Ride the button both ways with your thumb when you test it; letting it snap up is what the book tells you not to do.
deepSteps.quote: Assemble in reverse order, being careful to contain the Spring and Plunger as the Magazine Bottom is slid and locked into place. After reassembly has been completed, test Magazine Follower to ensure it has free movement.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® MARK II AUTOLOADING PISTOLS STANDARD, TARGET, GOVERNMENT TARGET, COMPETITION, AND 22/45 MODELS — AP & KAP 1/03 C R8 — Magazine Disassembly, reassembly, p.24
deepSteps.warn: Always ‘ride’ the Magazine Follower Button up and down with your thumb. Do not lower Follower Button and then permit it to snap up.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Run a solvent-wetted patch through the bore several times
Follow with a solvent-wetted bristle brush, back and forth the full length of the bore, until the grease and dirt are out of the bore and chamber
Dry patches until clean, then look down the bore
Grease left in the chamber interferes with feeding, so clean the chamber and extractor as often as it builds up
Finish with a dry patch, then one very lightly oiled
⛔ Before firing, remove all oil and grease from the bore

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Powder solvent on a clean patch or bristle brush: powder residue off every part of the mechanism
Give the bolt face, the extractor and the feed ramp particular attention
Wipe every surface clean with a cloth, then wipe it with a very lightly oiled patch or cloth
⚠ Confirm the firing pin stop, a small pin, is still in the bolt

cleaning.name: GRIP FRAME & MAINSPRING HOUSING
tasks: Wipe the grip frame, the magazine well and the mainspring housing clean
Only a light film of oil on moving parts: excess oil collects dust and dirt and can congeal in cold weather

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: If the magazine is dirty, strip and clean it (Deep Clean)
Check the follower moves freely and the spring tension is adequate
Check the magazine lips are free of nicks and burrs and are not deformed
Do not use a damaged, non-standard or improperly assembled magazine
Do not spray or apply lubricant directly on ammunition

reassembly: Make certain the pistol is free of cartridges, put the safety in the "off" (F) position, and set the hammer in its horizontal (cocked) position. Finger off the trigger.

Set the barrel-receiver on top of the frame so the square lug engages the square front recess under the receiver, and push it rearward until it stops with the rear of the receiver slightly overhanging the rear of the grip frame. If hand pressure will not seat it, strike the muzzle with a plastic or wood mallet only, without damaging the muzzle.
Muzzle up, pull the trigger: gravity returns the hammer to cocked if it was knocked down while the barrel went on.

⛔ Before the bolt goes in, be certain the firing pin stop (a small pin) is in the bolt. Without it the first trigger pull sends the firing pin far enough forward to dent the rear of the chamber and ruin the pistol. Then slide the bolt, recoil spring upward, fully into the receiver.

Point the muzzle at the ground, angle the rear of the pistol forward and slightly downward, and pull the trigger. The hammer falls to its uncocked position; you can see it through the slot in the rear of the grip frame and hear the click. Release the trigger. Every later step depends on this one.

Hold the pistol and the housing assembly horizontal and press the bolt stop pin up through the holes in the receiver and bolt until its tip stands above the top of the receiver. It must be fully in or the latch will not close.

Except on 22/45 models: check the hammer strut hangs down inside the housing slot and is not trapped behind the crosspin in the grip frame. If it is trapped, point the muzzle forward and pull the trigger again, or ease the strut over the crosspin with a small screwdriver blade.

Turn the pistol over and hold the trigger back with your thumb. Lift the housing so the end of the hammer strut goes into the oval cut inside it; you should feel spring pressure just before it shuts. Snap the latch closed.

Pull the bolt back: it should open fully. If it does not, open the latch, take out the housing and repeat from the hammer-drop step. A housing that pulls out as you swing it means the barrel-receiver is not fully rearward on the frame; one that is very hard to close usually means the hammer is still cocked.
Empty magazine in, pistol pointed in a safe direction, pull the trigger to uncock it. Ruger's rule is that a pistol is not stored loaded or cocked.
fncheck: With the pistol empty and pointed in a safe direction, pull the bolt back: Ruger's test of a correct reassembly is that it opens fully. If it moves only a fraction of an inch, the housing went in with the hammer in the wrong position, so open the latch and repeat the reassembly from the hammer-drop step. Then put the empty magazine in and pull the trigger to uncock it. Ruger's book publishes no other function test; anything that will not work as described goes to Ruger's Product Service Department.
